raw_response:
I've been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life. My husband passed a few years ago, my children are in the city — it's just me now, and I have about 7 mu left that I still work. I'm 70, my back isn't what it was, so I call the village machinery station for the big jobs. But I know this land. I know what it needs.

I'm planting what I've always planted: winter wheat on 6 mu, then summer corn on the same land right after harvest in June. That rotation, wheat in October and corn in summer — that's what keeps this family fed and gives me something to sell. I won't change that. My neighbor tried cotton years back and lost money. I'm not taking chances.

For seeds, I'll buy the improved wheat variety from the county seed station — Jimai 22 if they have it, or whatever the cooperative is selling. For corn I always use hybrid seed,郑单958 or similar. It yields better, worth the extra cost.

Fertilizer — I put down compound fertilizer as base before planting, then urea when the wheat is jointing. I know people say we use too much, but I'd rather not lose yield. I water the wheat three times: before winter sets in, at jointing, and when the grain is filling. Corn I water once if rain is short.

I'll keep 1 mu for garlic behind the house, planted this autumn. That's mostly for the family and to sell a bit at market.
